newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Indonesian asylum-seekers riot in Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian asylum-seekers riot in Malaysia.

text.p: More than 50 political asylum-seekers from Aceh province on Indonesia's Sumatra island rioted at a Malaysian camp for illegal immigrants on Tuesday against forcible deportation, witnesses said.

Police used tear gas and batons to quell the riot at Langkap camp in the north Malaysian state of Perak, before loading the protesters on to several trucks, the witnesses told Reuters at the scene. The police at the site declined to comment on the incident.

"They used tear gas. And then the police attacked them (the inmates). All we could hear was their shouts and cries," said Iqlil Tengku Ilias Leube, a Malaysia-based Acehnese businessman who was at the scene.
The witnesses said the trucks were believed to be taking the inmates to Port Klang near Kuala Lumpur, where two Indonesian ships were waiting to take them back.

Since March 1992, hundreds of Acehnese have fled across the Malacca Strait separating Sumatra and Malaysia to escape fighting between the Indonesian army and Aceh Merdeka (Free Aceh), a pro-independence movement for the province.

About 600 Acehnese have been detained in Malaysia since 1992, together with other Indonesian illegal immigrants who had come to the country in search of jobs. Malaysia has not recognised the Acehnese as political asylum-seekers and has said it will persuade them to return home.
